about.title: Patterson Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: A fall at a Patterson grocery store, gas station along Sperry Avenue, or apartment complex near 2nd Street can leave you dealing with pain, missed work, and a pile of questions about who's responsible. California law puts the burden on you to show the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard that caused your fall and didn't fix it or warn you. That's why what happens in the hours and days after your fall matters so much — photos of the spill, ice patch, broken step, or torn carpet, along with any surveillance footage before it's erased, can make or break a claim. Stanislaus County properties, like anywhere, vary in how quickly they respond to hazards, and an independent attorney can help sort out what the evidence actually shows. LawProactive connects Patterson residents with attorneys who handle these cases on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires proof the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help identify what evidence establishes that notice before it disappears.

items.title: Video Doesn't Last Forever
items.desc: Many Patterson businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly gives an attorney a real chance to request and preserve that footage.

items.title: Comparative Fault Works Both Ways
items.desc: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover even if you're partly at fault, though it can reduce what you're owed. An attorney can help present the facts in a way that reflects the full picture, not just the property owner's version.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Patterson?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. That window can be shorter if a government-owned property, like a Stanislaus County building, was involved, so it's worth getting evidence and legal guidance sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I didn't take photos right after my fall?
items.answer: It's not ideal, but it's not necessarily fatal to a claim. An attorney can still pursue incident reports, witness statements, and surveillance footage from the property, especially from higher-traffic spots along corridors like Sperry Avenue or Las Palmas Avenue where businesses often have cameras.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to get connected and ask questions.
